conventions.convention: For restricted labels, node residues are c−r modulo p; boundary nodes are read top to bottom, addable nodes give +, removable nodes give −, and reduction cancels −+ pairs. Good is the first surviving −; cogood is the last surviving +.
D(μ) uses restricted dual-Specht labels: in the group specialization D(μ) ≅ D^{μ′} ⊗ sign. Conjugation and sign twisting must both be retained.

JM projectors select generalized primary spaces. Content classes are residue multisets, and each distinct sequence representing a content is summed once. Restriction at rank zero is zero, S₀ is trivial, and induction to rank one has only residue zero.

Root-interval matching requires only the specified pointwise bound, not order preservation between different sources. Zero tests are modulo p; dimensions, cardinalities and character inversion are ordinary integers. Auxiliary dominant weights need not be restricted.

Restriction multiplicity is zero off normality and counts normal nodes weakly below the deleted restricted-label node on normality. Induction multiplicity is zero off conormality and counts conormal nodes weakly above the added node on conormality.

The first level consists of all weights whose last coordinate is one. Right Schur-module suppliers are converted through star; their regular corner gives same-shape Murphy modules. Exact projection preserves multiplicities only for surviving restricted simple labels.

General Hecke endpoints use (Tⱼ−q)(Tⱼ+1)=0 and additive JM eigenvalues [i]q. Finite quantum characteristic e may be composite; a temporary square-root extension is descended using absolute simplicity and finite Hom matrices.

The large example uses Brundan's r−c residues and ordinary Specht modules of conjugate shape. Its source simple is D_M(λ)^θ, with θ(Tⱼ)=q−1−Tⱼ; quantum characteristic four is not field characteristic four.

load_bearing.statement: For a field F of characteristic p>0, N≥2, a dominant polynomial highest weight μ, and every 1≤r≤s<N, the explicitly constructed T_{r,s}(J)v indexed by essential J form a basis of the simple weight space at μ−αᵣ−⋯−αₛ. Its dimension εₐ(r,s) satisfies εₐ(r,s)=νₐ(r,s)+Σ_{u=r+1}^s ε′ₐ(r,u−1)νₐ(u,s), where ε′ₐ(r,t)=ε_{a+ωₜ}(r,t). No restrictedness condition is imposed on μ or shifted auxiliary weights.

Let k have characteristic p>0, μ be p-restricted, and φᵢ(μ)>0. If B is its cogood i-node and ν=μ∪B, then FᵢD(μ) has simple socle and simple head, both D(ν), and total ungraded multiplicity [FᵢD(μ):D(ν)]=φᵢ(μ).

Over every field of characteristic p>0, the commuting JM elements admit prime-field simultaneous primary idempotents. Their content sums are central, the nonzero content sums are precisely block idempotents, and the subgroup-centralizing functor projectors give exact additive decompositions Res M=⊕ᵢEᵢM and Ind M=⊕ᵢFᵢM, compatible with contragredient duality.

For a field k of characteristic p>0, a p-regular λ, and a removable A whose deletion remains p-regular, the multiplicity of D^{λ−A} in Res D^λ is zero when A is not normal in the explicitly transposed restricted-signature convention. When A is normal it is one plus the number of same-residue normal removable nodes strictly above A.

For any field F and invertible q of finite quantum characteristic e≥2, with actual restricted Murphy simple labels and [i]q-primary functors, nonzero residue restrictions have simple socle and head given by good deletion, and nonzero residue inductions have simple socle and head given by cogood addition, each once. Each functor vanishes exactly when its selected move is undefined. This asserts endpoints, not total composition multiplicities.
For k of characteristic p>0 and a p-restricted μ of d≥1, soc_{S_{d−1}}(Res D(μ))=⊕_{i:εᵢ(μ)>0}D(μ−Aᵢ), where Aᵢ is the good i-node. The sum is multiplicity-free over distinct simple modules.

Good deletion and cogood addition define partial operators on p-restricted partitions, preserve restrictedness, change rank by minus or plus one, and satisfy μ=ẽfᵢν if and only if ν=ẽeᵢμ on their domains.

For every commutative unital ring R and n≥0, every element of Z(RSₙ) is an R-linear combination of evaluations of integral monomial symmetric polynomials at the JM elements. Conversely every symmetric polynomial evaluation is central. No integer is inverted.

concerns.concern: The Convention warning says a node is normal here 'exactly when its transposed node is normal in Brundan's sense for the transpose partition'. This is false for the stated signature. At p=3 take μ=(3,3,2,1,1) and A=(2,3): its residue-1 word is −+ at (2,3),(4,2), so A is not normal. In μ′=(5,3,2), Brundan's transposed node (3,2) has empty demand/support sets and is normal. Both partitions are 3-restricted. The same-shape Brundan lattice test agrees with the present signature, with negated color names. His transpose comparison concerns his labels versus Kleshchev's older convention, not this newly fixed signature: [Brundan, §§2.3–2.4](https://pages.uoregon.edu/brundan/papers/quantum.pdf), printed p. 4.

F5 repeats the false assertion that the signature-normal nodes of λ′ are exactly the transposes of the Brundan-normal nodes of λ. The preceding counterexample applies with λ=(5,3,2). Step 2.1 invokes F5. The first-level supplier instead explicitly defines ordinary normality by transposing into this batch's restricted signature, which does support the intended count. These two notions must not be identified with Brundan's same-shape lattice normality.

F1 calls the translation to the parent convention 'the transposed-node dictionary of Remark 2.4(II)'. For the actual parent signature, the displayed Brundan normal/good rows correspond on the same shape with residue signs reversed. F2 correctly uses the same-shape θ-twist for the module comparison, and the numerical tables and decomposition conclusions check out. Align F1 with that comparison and the corrected signature warning.
